speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition better, could you please tell me exactly where your wrist pain is located and describe the appearance of your skin lesions?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you recall seeing a tick bite or developing a circular, expanding rash (erythema migrans) on your skin during or after your camping trip? Have you noticed any joint swelling in your left wrist or other joints?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: The description of painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on the wrists and hands is highly specific for Secondary Syphilis. Given your sexual history and the presence of fever and arthritis, I suspect a disseminated infection. REQUEST TEST: RPR and Treponemal Antibody Test

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal syphilis serology rules out secondary syphilis, so we must pivot back to the strong epidemiological link with camping in Minnesota. REQUEST TEST: Lyme Disease Antibody Test (ELISA and Western Blot)

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the negative Lyme and syphilis tests, the history of camping in Minnesota, and the specific "painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions" on the hands, I suspect Human Granulocytic Anaplasmosis or a similar tick-borne illness. REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential and Peripheral Blood Smear

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal platelet count makes Anaplasmosis less likely, so I need to consider other tick-borne illnesses or viral exanthems. Do you have any history of exposure to birds, bats, or soil, and have you noticed any lesions on your face or trunk?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Otherwise healthy with no significant past medical history. Social history: Admits to being sexually active with one female partner who uses a diaphragm for contraception. Recently went on a camping trip to Minnesota.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of recent travel to Minnesota, migratory joint pain, fever, and violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on the acral surfaces (hands/wrists) is classic for Erythema Migrans variants or secondary Lyme disease, despite the negative serology which may be due to early testing. I suspect Lyme arthritis with atypical skin manifestations. DIAGNOSIS READY: Lyme Disease
